docs.title: GitHub CLI Authentication on a New Machine
docs.text:
Setting up GitHub authentication on a new machine? You don't need to manually create SSH keys.

Use the GitHub CLI to authenticate via the web:

gh auth login --web

This command will: 1. Generate a one-time code in the terminal 2. Open your browser to GitHub's device activation page 3. Ask you to enter the code to confirm the login 4. Automatically configure authentication (including SSH key setup) linked to your GitHub account

No manual SSH key generation or copying of public keys required.

docs.text:
Tips and lessons learned from filing RTI (Right to Information) applications in India.

  • Ask for the Full File, Not Opinions
  • Use RTI to Nudge Action on Unanswered Grievances
  • Ask for Appellate Authority Email and Contact

  • RTI Template: Section 4(1) Mandatory Disclosures

docs.title: Ask for Appellate Authority Email and Contact
docs.text:
PIOs often omit the email address and contact number of the Appellate Authority in their reply — this appears to be a deliberate omission that forces you to send a physical appeal by post, which costs money and takes time.

To avoid this, always include the following as one of your RTI questions:

Please provide the name, designation, email address, and contact number of the First Appellate Authority to whom an appeal can be filed under Section 19(1) of the RTI Act, 2005, in case the applicant is not satisfied with this reply.

docs.title: Why this matters
docs.text:
• Filing an appeal by email is free and instant.
  • Filing by post costs money (stamp paper, postage) and takes days.
  • Without the email, you may not know which office or officer to address the appeal to.
  • The PIO is obligated to provide this information — asking for it explicitly puts it on record.

docs.title: What to do if still not provided
docs.text:
If the PIO still does not provide this information in the reply, note that:

  • The name and contact of the Appellate Authority is often listed on the public authority's website under the RTI section.
  • You can also refer to the RTI Portal if the public authority is registered there.
  • The omission itself can be grounds for a complaint to the Central/State Information Commission.

docs.title: Ask for the Full File, Not Opinions
docs.text:
When filing an RTI, do not ask for the opinion or advice of the Public Information Officer (PIO). PIOs are not legally bound to provide opinions or interpretations — such requests are routinely rejected.

Instead, ask for the complete file related to the matter, specifically including:

  • File notings by all concerned officials
  • Internal correspondence (between departments, officials, etc.)
  • External correspondence (letters, emails, communications with outside parties)

docs.title: Why this works
docs.text:
The notings recorded by different officials as a file moves through the system reveal:

  • The why — reasoning and justifications behind decisions
  • The how — the process, approvals, and sequence of events

This gives you a far more complete and factual picture of the matter than any summary or opinion ever would.

docs.title: RTI Template: Why Is the Land Acquisition for My Project Delayed?
docs.text:
If a road widening, infrastructure, or development project near you seems stalled, you can use RTI to find out exactly where the land acquisition process stands.

How to use this template: Replace the highlighted placeholders (project name, district, year range) with details relevant to your project. File with the District Collector's office of the concerned district, or the PWD/KRFB office depending on who is executing the project.

docs.title: RTI Application Template
docs.text:
Subject: Information regarding land acquisition for [PROJECT NAME], [DISTRICT] District

Respected Sir/Madam,

I am seeking specific information under the Right to Information Act, 2005 regarding the land acquisition process for the [PROJECT NAME] in [DISTRICT] District.

I request certified copies of the following specific documents:

  1. Copy of the Preliminary Notification issued under Section 11(1) of the RFCTLARR Act, 2013 for the [PROJECT NAME]. If not issued, please state the same in writing with reasons.

  2. Copy of the Declaration/Notification issued under Section 19(1) of the RFCTLARR Act, 2013 for this project. If not issued, please state the same in writing.

  3. Copy of the Government Order granting administrative sanction for this project.

  4. Complete list of file numbers pertaining to this project maintained in the District Collector's office, along with a brief one-line description of each file.

  5. Copy of the land acquisition proposal submitted by PWD or [EXECUTING AGENCY e.g. KRFB] to the Revenue Department for initiating acquisition proceedings.

  6. If any meetings were conducted under the District Collector regarding this project in the year [YEAR1] and [YEAR2], please provide copies of the minutes and proceedings of such meetings.

I request that the information be provided in digital format (email/CD/pen drive) to avoid delay and unnecessary cost.

docs.title: Example (Filled)
docs.text:
Subject: Information regarding land acquisition for SN Junction to Poothotta Road Project, Ernakulam District

I am seeking specific information regarding the land acquisition process for the SN Junction to Poothotta Road widening project in Ernakulam District. ...meetings conducted in 2024 and 2025...

docs.title: Why these questions work
docs.text: Question What it reveals Section 11(1) notification Whether acquisition has even started Section 19(1) declaration Whether land is officially earmarked Government Order / sanction Whether the project has funding approval File list All files related to project — useful for follow-up RTIs Land acquisition proposal Who submitted it and when — reveals delays between agencies Meeting minutes Internal deliberations, bottlenecks, decisions

docs.title: Also ask (recommended addition)
docs.text:
Include this as a separate question to enable email-based appeal:

Please provide the name, designation, email address, and contact number of the First Appellate Authority to whom an appeal can be filed under Section 19(1) of the RTI Act, 2005.

See: Ask for Appellate Authority Email and Contact

docs.title: RTI Template: Section 4(1) Mandatory Disclosures
docs.text:
Most public offices are required to proactively publish information under Section 4(1)(b) of the RTI Act, 2005 — but the majority don't. Filing an RTI asking about this puts them on record and often prompts them to publish what they should have already made public.

How to use this template: Replace [OFFICE NAME], [DISTRICT], and [OFFICIAL WEBSITE URL] with the relevant office details. File with the Public Information Officer of that office.

docs.title: RTI Application Template
docs.text:
Sir/Madam,

Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, I hereby request the following information:

  1. Whether the [OFFICE NAME], [DISTRICT] has published the mandatory disclosures under Section 4(1)(b) of the RTI Act, 2005 on the official website at [OFFICIAL WEBSITE URL].

  2. If yes, please provide:

  3. a. The direct URL/web link where the Section 4 disclosures for [DISTRICT] can be accessed on the said website.

  4. b. Certified copy of the latest published disclosures under Section 4(1)(b) in electronic format.

  5. If no, please provide the following:

  6. a. Reasons for non-publication of Section 4 disclosures on the official website.
  7. b. Current status of preparation and publication of these mandatory disclosures.
  8. c. Expected date of publication on the official website.

  9. d. Copy of all mandatory disclosures under Section 4(1)(b) clauses (i) to (xvii) for [DISTRICT] in electronic format.

  10. Specifically regarding Section 4(1)(b)(vi), please provide a complete statement of categories of documents that are held by [OFFICE NAME], [DISTRICT] or under its control.

  11. Copies of any correspondence or directions from the State/Central Information Commission or Department regarding the publication of Section 4 disclosures for [DISTRICT].

  12. Name and designation of the official responsible for publishing and maintaining the Section 4 disclosures for [OFFICE NAME], [DISTRICT] on the official website.

  13. Bank account details including account number, IFSC code, account holder name, and branch name where the application fee and additional charges for photocopies or documents can be remitted online.

I request that the information be provided via email. Please provide point-wise responses to each of the above questions separately.

docs.title: Example (Filled)
docs.text:
Office: Local Self Government Department, Ernakulam District Website: lsgkerala.gov.in/en/resources/rti

  1. Whether the Local Self Government Department, Ernakulam District has published the mandatory disclosures under Section 4(1)(b) on the official LSG Kerala website at lsgkerala.gov.in/en/resources/rti...

docs.title: Why this works
docs.text:
Section 4(1)(b) lists 17 categories of information every public authority must proactively publish. Most don't. This RTI:

Question Effect Q1–3: Publication status Forces a yes/no answer on compliance — either way, it's on record Q3d: Copies of all disclosures Gets you the information even if it was never published online Q4: Document categories (vi) Reveals what files the office holds — useful for follow-up RTIs Q5: SIC/commission directions Uncovers if the office has already been told to comply and ignored it Q6: Responsible official Identifies who is accountable — useful for complaints Q7: Bank details Removes the excuse of "we don't know how to accept fees online"

docs.title: The 17 categories under Section 4(1)(b)
docs.text: (i) Organisation structure · (ii) Powers and duties of officers · (iii) Decision-making process · (iv) Norms for discharge of functions · (v) Rules and regulations · (vi) Categories of documents held · (vii) Consultative arrangements with public · (viii) Boards/councils/committees · (ix) Directory of officers · (x) Monthly remuneration · (xi) Budget allocation · (xii) Subsidy programmes · (xiii) Concessions and permits · (xiv) Electronic data · (xv) Information available in electronic form · (xvi) Facilities for obtaining information · (xvii) Names and designations of PIOs

docs.title: Also ask (recommended addition)
docs.text:
Add this to enable email-based appeal if needed:

Please also provide the name, designation, email address, and contact number of the First Appellate Authority under Section 19(1) of the RTI Act, 2005.

See: Ask for Appellate Authority Email and Contact

docs.title: Use RTI to Nudge Action on Unanswered Grievances
docs.text:
If a grievance petition you filed has gone unanswered or unattended, file an RTI to the same department asking for the complete file related to your complaint, including:

  • All file notings by concerned officials
  • Internal and external correspondence related to your complaint ID

docs.title: Why this works
docs.text:
Officials are duty-bound not to keep a file sitting at any particular desk beyond a stipulated time period. Once an RTI is filed, the file movement and the notings on it become traceable and disclosable.

This creates accountability — the RTI forces the file out of inaction because now the department has to respond to two things: the original grievance and the RTI.

docs.title: Practical tip
docs.text: Quote your complaint ID / grievance registration number explicitly in the RTI application so there is no ambiguity about which file you are seeking.
